executiveSummary: The protocol demonstrated high resilience with a final score of 91/100, maintaining price stability despite coordinated governance spamming and significant arbitrage pressure. While the final price appreciated by 1.6%, the system is currently vulnerable to governance fatigue due to low proposal thresholds and lack of staking locks. The high Gini coefficient of 0.346 indicates a concentration of power that, while currently benign, allows whales to dominate every proposal cycle without economic friction.

failureModes.name: Governance Proposal Spamming
failureModes.description: The low proposal threshold of 0.1% allowed a group of governance attackers to flood the system with proposals (11 through 164) starting at tick 6. This creates a noise-to-signal ratio that can mask malicious upgrades or exhaust legitimate voter participation.

failureModes.name: Arbitrage-Induced Volatility
failureModes.description: A price spike to $1.0516 triggered a massive sell-off by arbitrageurs, causing a rapid correction back to $1.0158. The lack of a cooldown penalty or withdrawal lock allowed these agents to exit positions instantly, stressing the liquidity pool.

attackVectors.label: Governance Capture and Saturation
timeline: GOV_01 through GOV_04 initiate a barrage of proposals starting at t=6 to t=8 to test quorum limits.
WHALE_01 through WHALE_13 begin a pattern of 'vote_yes' on virtually every proposal regardless of content.
HOLDER_05 and HOLDER_07 join the voting block at t=27, cementing a permanent majority that ignores proposal substance.
By t=29, GOV_01 and GOV_02 are submitting proposals (0, 1) that are passed instantly by the whale bloc.

recommendations.rationale: Increasing the threshold would prevent agents like GOV_01 from spamming the network with low-stake proposals.
Implementing a lock period would prevent arbitrageurs like ARB_06 from instantly dumping tokens acquired through yield or market fluctuations.
A penalty on immediate unstaking would reduce the profitability of the short-term sell-offs seen between t=17 and t=20.

comparison.reasoning: The simulation mirrors the 'Curve Wars' where large holders (Whales) and protocol aggregators (Gov Attackers) dominate the voting layer to control protocol direction, though without a death spiral.
